bull_bear.body:
- Long-standing relationships with OEMs, state-of-the-art facilities and best-in-class processes that help deliver superior value to customers; customer surveys are conducted periodically to capture feedback
- Diversity of product portfolio across steering, engine, braking and transmission components, which management cites as a mitigant to technology obsolescence
- Enhanced R&D capabilities with localisation of testing and validation capabilities
- Products serve a variety of vehicle businesses experiencing different levels of technology adoption, spreading exposure across segments
- Established export franchise - Steering & Linkages exports grew 27.7% in FY26 and the business recorded its highest-ever sales, aided by ramp-up of new business programs
- Overseas distribution network for brake/aftermarket exports being extended into new geographies in the US, Africa and Middle East
- Skilled workforce backed by a dedicated training centre and job-skill enhancement training, with Quality DOJO implementation in progress across plants
- Part of the Rane Group and a subsidiary of Rane Holdings Limited, with access to group joint ventures such as ZF Rane Automotive India Private Limited
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Industry / market concentration on the Indian automotive sector — A major portion of revenue is derived from the Indian automotive sector, so any drop in vehicle production will have a significant impact on the Company's business. Management is responding by increasing revenue from international markets, adding new products to grow organic revenue and diversifying customers across vehicle businesses.
- Price-down pressure on newly secured products — Management flags in the same risk row that new products secured by the Company are at significantly lower sale prices and pose a significant risk in terms of profitability; the Company is pursuing dialogue with customers for price increases against the global environment and increasing cost pressures.
- Technology obsolescence in the auto component portfolio — Changes in the auto industry and customer preference can render technology obsolete. Mitigants cited are enhanced R&D capabilities, localisation of testing and validation, and a portfolio spread across steering, engine, braking and transmission components serving vehicle businesses at different levels of technology adoption.
- Competition, including from unorganised players — Maintaining market share in competitive markets and the availability of unorganised players pose a challenge; the Company relies on long-standing OEM relationships, its facilities and processes, and periodic customer surveys.
- Raw material (input) price volatility — Material cost is a significant part of total cost and volatility in raw material prices will erode margin. Mitigation is via cost reduction through alternate sourcing and localisation, negotiating pass-through of input cost increases to customers, and process and yield improvements.
- Foreign currency exposure on exports and imported raw materials — The Company exports products to various countries and imports raw materials, exposing it to exchange-rate risk. It balances imports and exports for a natural hedge, works with customers to index prices, and takes forwards on a rolling basis to protect export realisation.
- Interest rate risk on borrowings used to fund expansion — Use of borrowings to fund expansion exposes the Company to interest rate risk; it manages this by maintaining optimal debt-equity levels, funding capex primarily through internal accruals, optimising working capital and leveraging banking relationships. The FY26 debt-equity ratio improved to 0.82 standalone from 1.10, aided by debt reduction from advance land sale proceeds.
- Quality and delivery risk on safety-critical components, and attrition of key personnel — Quality and delivery are described as sacrosanct for the safety-critical products supplied by the Group, with Quality DOJO being rolled out across plants to lift workforce skills; separately, attrition of key personnel could impact business operations and growth, addressed through HR processes, a dedicated training centre and leadership pipeline development.

business.body: The business of the Company is manufacturing and marketing of auto components for the transportation industry, viz., steering and suspension linkage products, steering gear products, aluminium alloy based high pressure die-casting products, brake components and engine components. It serves Indian and overseas OEMs across passenger vehicles, commercial vehicles, farm tractors and two-wheelers, and also sells into the automotive aftermarket through a distribution network. Following the Scheme of Amalgamation with erstwhile Rane Engine Valve Limited and erstwhile Rane Brake Lining Limited, the Company now reports as an amalgamated entity spanning five businesses: Steering & Linkages, Light Metal Castings, Engine Components, Brake Components and Aftermarket Products.

outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The routed bundle carries no named capex project, capacity addition, commissioning or ramp-up plan. The only footprint disclosure is in Corporate Information, which states Plant Locations of 15 in India and 1 outside India (through subsidiary). The overseas footprint sits in two subsidiaries - Rane (Madras) International Holdings B.V., The Netherlands, which holds the Company's foreign strategic investments, and Rane Automotive Components Mexico S de R.L. de C.V., which is in the business of steering and linkage auto components; total investments as on March 31, 2026 by the Company in RACM and RMIH are MXN$ 19.03 million and Euro 4.32 million respectively. On funding stance, the MD&A risk table states that borrowings are used to fund expansion and that the Company manages interest rate risk by maintaining optimal debt-equity levels and by doing 'Capex primarily through internal accruals', constantly optimising working capital to reduce interest costs. Capacity-adjacent operational initiatives mentioned are the Quality DOJO rollout across plants and the RMSP 4.0 framework, under which 102 Productivity, Quality, Cost, Delivery and Safety improvement projects were completed during the year. The Company's scale expanded through the Scheme of Amalgamation with erstwhile Rane Engine Valve Limited and erstwhile Rane Brake Lining Limited (shares allotted April 23, 2025) rather than through a disclosed greenfield project.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Indian auto component industry demand: ACMA data showed H1 FY26 industry turnover up 6.8% YoY, OEM supplies up 7.3% led by PV and LCV, and exports up 9.3%; GST rate reduction flowing into stronger vehicle demand in H2 FY 2025-26 is expected to build further momentum
- GST 2.0 reform (small PV and two-wheelers up to 350cc cut from 28% to 18%, auto components aligned at 18%) has meaningfully improved affordability across mass-market segments and is expected to sustain consumption-led growth into FY 2026-27
- Structural transformation of the component industry - rising vehicle penetration, higher technology content per vehicle, accelerating EV adoption, tightening emission norms and mainstreaming of ADAS - creating incremental demand for precision-engineered components; the industry has potential to nearly double by 2030
- Domestic vehicle production tailwind in FY26: PV production at a record (+9%), M&HCV +16%, LCV +11%, farm tractors +24% and two-wheelers +12% (SIAM), with rural recovery and policy support cited as drivers
- Aftermarket as a growth engine - a large and rapidly expanding vehicle parc, formalisation and largely non-discretionary replacement spend drove ~9% YoY aftermarket growth in H1 FY26, with India expected to be the fastest-growing aftermarket in the region
- 'China plus one' supply-chain shift - India's cost competitiveness, engineering talent pool and improving logistics position it as a preferred sourcing partner as global OEMs diversify, opening space to capture incremental share in international networks
- Export environment improving after the US-India trade framework removed the additional 25% penalty and temporarily set the reciprocal rate at 10% w.e.f. February 24, 2026, restoring export competitiveness, though specific tariffs on steel, aluminium and select automotive components remain
- Near-term headwinds management flags: Middle East war and Strait of Hormuz exposure driving energy, freight and insurance costs and currency weakness; input cost volatility in steel, aluminium, precious and rare-earth metals and semiconductors; trade protectionism and tariff uncertainty; affordability pressure in mass vehicle segments and uneven rural income recovery
- Global backdrop turning more challenging - 2026 global light vehicle sales forecast broadly flat with production expected to edge down about 0.4%, OEMs accelerating supply-chain regionalisation, cost optimisation and flexible powertrain strategies
- Medium-term Indian outlook described as decisively positive - PV supported by utility vehicles and alternative powertrains (CNG, hybrid, electric), two-wheelers by rural demand, financing and premiumisation, and CV linked to economic activity and replacement with buses expected to outperform
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: Rane (Madras) Limited is a Rane Holdings-controlled Indian auto-component maker supplying steering and suspension linkages, steering gears, aluminium high-pressure die-castings, brake components and engine components to OEMs and the aftermarket, operating 15 plants in India and one overseas through a subsidiary.

open.item: With effect from June 01, 2026 the Board approved designation changes making Ms. Gowri Kailasam Executive Director for the Engine Components and Aftermarket Products Divisions (additionally leading the Steering and Gears Division of group JV ZF Rane Automotive India Private Limited) and Mr. Aditya Ganesh Executive Director for the Steering & Linkage and Light Metal Castings Divisions.
Light Metal Castings Business expects strong export demand in FY 2026-27 supported by ramp-up from new programme launches, with the domestic market expected to remain stable.

In brake components the Company continues initiatives to sustain organic sales and enhance export turnover through the overseas distribution network by entering new geographies in the US, Africa and Middle East, supported by an enhanced product range, new grades and regulatory product certifications.

To mitigate dependence on the Indian automotive sector, the Company is working to increase revenue from international markets, add new products to grow organic revenue and diversify customers across vehicle businesses, and is pursuing price increases with customers against rising cost pressures.

The Aftermarket Products business, restructured in FY26, is driving synergy across product lines, demand at retailer level, increased promotion, new product introductions and digital tools to improve efficiency and market penetration.
Implementation of Quality DOJO across the plants is in progress to improve workforce skills and mitigate quality and delivery risk.
The Company intends to fund capex primarily through internal accruals while maintaining optimal debt-equity levels and optimising working capital to reduce interest costs.

- GST 2.0 reform (small PV and two-wheelers up to 350cc cut from 28% to 18%, auto components aligned at 18%) has meaningfully improved affordability across mass-market segments and is expected to sustain consumption-led growth into FY 2026-27
- Structural transformation of the component industry - rising vehicle penetration, higher technology content per vehicle, accelerating EV adoption, tightening emission norms and mainstreaming of ADAS - creating incremental demand for precision-engineered components; the industry has potential to nearly double by 2030
- Domestic vehicle production tailwind in FY26: PV production at a record (+9%), M&HCV +16%, LCV +11%, farm tractors +24% and two-wheelers +12% (SIAM), with rural recovery and policy support cited as drivers
- Aftermarket as a growth engine - a large and rapidly expanding vehicle parc, formalisation and largely non-discretionary replacement spend drove ~9% YoY aftermarket growth in H1 FY26, with India expected to be the fastest-growing aftermarket in the region
- 'China plus one' supply-chain shift - India's cost competitiveness, engineering talent pool and improving logistics position it as a preferred sourcing partner as global OEMs diversify, opening space to capture incremental share in international networks
- Export environment improving after the US-India trade framework removed the additional 25% penalty and temporarily set the reciprocal rate at 10% w.e.f. February 24, 2026, restoring export competitiveness, though specific tariffs on steel, aluminium and select automotive components remain
- Near-term headwinds management flags: Middle East war and Strait of Hormuz exposure driving energy, freight and insurance costs and currency weakness; input cost volatility in steel, aluminium, precious and rare-earth metals and semiconductors; trade protectionism and tariff uncertainty; affordability pressure in mass vehicle segments and uneven rural income recovery
- Global backdrop turning more challenging - 2026 global light vehicle sales forecast broadly flat with production expected to edge down about 0.4%, OEMs accelerating supply-chain regionalisation, cost optimisation and flexible powertrain strategies
- Medium-term Indian outlook described as decisively positive - PV supported by utility vehicles and alternative powertrains (CNG, hybrid, electric), two-wheelers by rural demand, financing and premiumisation, and CV linked to economic activity and replacement with buses expected to outperform

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Complete integration as an amalgamated entity: following the Scheme of Amalgamation with erstwhile Rane Engine Valve Limited and erstwhile Rane Brake Lining Limited, the Company allotted 1,13,71,870 equity shares on April 23, 2025 and now operates the combined steering, linkage, light metal castings, engine and brake component businesses under one listed entity
- Realign divisional leadership around the enlarged portfolio - with effect from June 01, 2026 an Executive Director leads Engine Components and Aftermarket Products (and additionally the Steering and Gears Division of group JV ZF Rane Automotive India Private Limited), while another Executive Director leads Steering & Linkage and Light Metal Castings
- Hold and use the overseas structure - two overseas subsidiaries, Rane (Madras) International Holdings B.V. (Netherlands, holding foreign strategic investments) and Rane Automotive Components Mexico S de R.L. de C.V. (steering and linkage components) - as the international manufacturing and investment platform
- Sustain the credit profile: CRISIL re-affirmed the Long-Term Rating at 'CRISIL A+ / stable' and the Short-Term Rating at 'CRISIL A1' during the year, citing expected sustained performance over the medium term

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The routed bundle carries no named capex project, capacity addition, commissioning or ramp-up plan. The only footprint disclosure is in Corporate Information, which states Plant Locations of 15 in India and 1 outside India (through subsidiary). The overseas footprint sits in two subsidiaries - Rane (Madras) International Holdings B.V., The Netherlands, which holds the Company's foreign strategic investments, and Rane Automotive Components Mexico S de R.L. de C.V., which is in the business of steering and linkage auto components; total investments as on March 31, 2026 by the Company in RACM and RMIH are MXN$ 19.03 million and Euro 4.32 million respectively. On funding stance, the MD&A risk table states that borrowings are used to fund expansion and that the Company manages interest rate risk by maintaining optimal debt-equity levels and by doing 'Capex primarily through internal accruals', constantly optimising working capital to reduce interest costs. Capacity-adjacent operational initiatives mentioned are the Quality DOJO rollout across plants and the RMSP 4.0 framework, under which 102 Productivity, Quality, Cost, Delivery and Safety improvement projects were completed during the year. The Company's scale expanded through the Scheme of Amalgamation with erstwhile Rane Engine Valve Limited and erstwhile Rane Brake Lining Limited (shares allotted April 23, 2025) rather than through a disclosed greenfield project.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Long-standing relationships with OEMs, state-of-the-art facilities and best-in-class processes that help deliver superior value to customers; customer surveys are conducted periodically to capture feedback
- Diversity of product portfolio across steering, engine, braking and transmission components, which management cites as a mitigant to technology obsolescence
- Enhanced R&D capabilities with localisation of testing and validation capabilities
- Products serve a variety of vehicle businesses experiencing different levels of technology adoption, spreading exposure across segments
- Established export franchise - Steering & Linkages exports grew 27.7% in FY26 and the business recorded its highest-ever sales, aided by ramp-up of new business programs
- Overseas distribution network for brake/aftermarket exports being extended into new geographies in the US, Africa and Middle East
- Skilled workforce backed by a dedicated training centre and job-skill enhancement training, with Quality DOJO implementation in progress across plants
- Part of the Rane Group and a subsidiary of Rane Holdings Limited, with access to group joint ventures such as ZF Rane Automotive India Private Limited

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- Industry / market concentration on the Indian automotive sector — A major portion of revenue is derived from the Indian automotive sector, so any drop in vehicle production will have a significant impact on the Company's business. Management is responding by increasing revenue from international markets, adding new products to grow organic revenue and diversifying customers across vehicle businesses.
- Price-down pressure on newly secured products — Management flags in the same risk row that new products secured by the Company are at significantly lower sale prices and pose a significant risk in terms of profitability; the Company is pursuing dialogue with customers for price increases against the global environment and increasing cost pressures.
- Technology obsolescence in the auto component portfolio — Changes in the auto industry and customer preference can render technology obsolete. Mitigants cited are enhanced R&D capabilities, localisation of testing and validation, and a portfolio spread across steering, engine, braking and transmission components serving vehicle businesses at different levels of technology adoption.
- Competition, including from unorganised players — Maintaining market share in competitive markets and the availability of unorganised players pose a challenge; the Company relies on long-standing OEM relationships, its facilities and processes, and periodic customer surveys.
- Raw material (input) price volatility — Material cost is a significant part of total cost and volatility in raw material prices will erode margin. Mitigation is via cost reduction through alternate sourcing and localisation, negotiating pass-through of input cost increases to customers, and process and yield improvements.
- Foreign currency exposure on exports and imported raw materials — The Company exports products to various countries and imports raw materials, exposing it to exchange-rate risk. It balances imports and exports for a natural hedge, works with customers to index prices, and takes forwards on a rolling basis to protect export realisation.
- Interest rate risk on borrowings used to fund expansion — Use of borrowings to fund expansion exposes the Company to interest rate risk; it manages this by maintaining optimal debt-equity levels, funding capex primarily through internal accruals, optimising working capital and leveraging banking relationships. The FY26 debt-equity ratio improved to 0.82 standalone from 1.10, aided by debt reduction from advance land sale proceeds.
- Quality and delivery risk on safety-critical components, and attrition of key personnel — Quality and delivery are described as sacrosanct for the safety-critical products supplied by the Group, with Quality DOJO being rolled out across plants to lift workforce skills; separately, attrition of key personnel could impact business operations and growth, addressed through HR processes, a dedicated training centre and leadership pipeline development.

themes.title: Auto components & EV-driveline localization
themes.need: Premiumization, content-per-vehicle rise and EV/hybrid transition pull a deep auto-ancillary chain - MOTHERSON/SONACOMS/BOSCHLTD/SCHAEFFLER/SKFINDIA/UNOMINDA-tier on driveline, bearings, wiring (MSUMI) and EV systems; OLAELEC/ATHERENERG/OLECTRA on EV OEMs (OLAELEC targeting cell-to-pack 10-15% cost edge); SUNDRMFAST/ENDURANCE/CRAFTSMAN/BHARATFORG on forgings/machining. Q1FY27 showed contracted pricing finally landing for Tier-2s: SSWL earned EBITDA/wheel of Rs 314 against Rs 262 YoY, which management attributed mostly to two years of OEM input-price increases finally landing (1-5%, more pending) rather than mix, with all plants above 95% utilisation and knuckles at 100%; KROSS delivered a 12.23% EBITDA margin (+63bps) BEFORE two retrospective pass-throughs land (steel settled ~15 July, the CV conversion-cost settlement still pending), making Q1 a floor rather than a peak.
themes.driver: GST 2.0 demand pull; retrospective OEM price pass-throughs still to land (KROSS CV conversion cost); EV cell/Gigafactory ramps (OLAELEC 6GWh by June); export + new-platform content wins.
